title: Global Desertification: Building a Science for Dryland Development
data_and_method: Review
finding: Reviews how dryland ecosystems and livelihoods function together and introduces the Drylands Development Paradigm as a framework for research and policy.

title: Desertification, land use, and the transformation of global drylands
venue: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
data_and_method: Conceptual framework
finding: Proposes treating desertification as state changes within a land use, and separating changes that reverse readily from regime shifts that persist.
note: Useful for deciding what our forecast target should count as degradation.

title: Accelerated dryland expansion under climate change
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Title claims accelerated dryland expansion under climate change.

title: Global ecosystem thresholds driven by aridity
data_and_method: 20 ecosystem attributes along aridity gradients
finding: Ecosystem attributes change abruptly at aridity values of 0.54, 0.7 and 0.8 (plant productivity, then soil fertility, then plant cover and richness). More than 20% of land is projected to cross at least one threshold by 2100.
note: Check how aridity is defined before comparing with aridity-index classes.

title: Anthropogenic climate change has driven over 5 million km2 of drylands towards desertification
data_and_method: Observation-based attribution separating climate change, climate variability, CO2 fertilisation and land use
finding: 6% of drylands desertified over the period. Anthropogenic climate change degraded 12.6% of drylands (5.43 million km2) despite average global greening.
note: A template for attribution methods.

title: Land in balance: The scientific conceptual framework for Land Degradation Neutrality
data_and_method: Conceptual framework from the UNCCD Science-Policy Interface
finding: Defines land degradation neutrality as no net loss of land-based natural capital against a baseline, with an avoid, reduce, reverse hierarchy.

title: Desertification
venue: Climate Change and Land: an IPCC special report (Chapter 3), Cambridge University Press
data_and_method: Assessment chapter of the IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Land
finding: The IPCC assessment of how climate change and desertification interact, with a confidence level for each statement. Rates early warning systems and remote sensing as high-return investments.
note: The DOI points to the 2022 Cambridge edition of the 2019 report.

title: Testing a non-equilibrium model of rangeland vegetation dynamics in Mongolia
region: Mongolia: desert steppe, steppe, mountain steppe
data_and_method: Field plots along grazing gradients in three zones
finding: Desert steppe vegetation varied between years with rainfall and not along grazing gradients, as the non-equilibrium model predicts. In the steppe and mountain steppe, grazing shifted cover from grasses toward forbs and weedy annuals.
note: Why grazing effects have to be considered by zone.

title: Global assessment of the non-equilibrium concept in rangelands
data_and_method: Review of 58 studies with a global map of rainfall variability
finding: Away from water points and key resources, grazing degradation was absent where the coefficient of variation of annual rainfall exceeds 33%. All studies without degradation had a CV above 33%.
note: Only 17 of 58 studies reported their own CV; the rest rely on a station map kriged over up to 2,000 km. The paper reports 41 of 58 sites as 84% (it is 71%). Jamsranjav et al. 2018 give a CV of 23-32% for Mongolia's forest steppe, eastern steppe and steppe and 34% for desert steppe.

title: A critical review of degradation assumptions applied to Mongolia’s Gobi Desert
data_and_method: Critical review with biophysical and social data
finding: Tests five common assumptions (too many animals, goats cause desertification, rainfall is declining, biomass is declining, rangelands are degraded) and finds they are not always supported.

title: Mongolian rangelands at a tipping point? Biomass and cover are stable but composition shifts and richness declines after 20 years of grazing and increasing temperatures
region: Mongolia: desert steppe, steppe, mountain steppe
data_and_method: Resampled field plots
finding: After 20 years of warming and higher stocking, biomass and cover were unchanged or higher, but species richness fell in the steppe and mountain steppe. The authors judge the degradation reversible.
note: Field evidence that cover and biomass can hold while composition degrades.

title: Applying a dryland degradation framework for rangelands: the case of Mongolia
data_and_method: 143 sites in 36 soums, indicators measured at increasing distance from winter corrals
finding: Livestock use had no effect on soils, richness or standing biomass and subtle effects on cover and palatable plants. Three national assessments agree that very severe degradation covers 1-18% of land, with most rangeland slightly (33-53%) or moderately (25-40%) degraded.
note: Field data are public on Dryad (doi:10.5061/dryad.3ch50).

title: Plant community change in three Mongolian steppe ecosystems 1994–2013: applications to state-and-transition models
region: Mongolia: desert steppe, steppe, mountain steppe
data_and_method: Repeated monitoring on grazing gradients; state-and-transition models
finding: Plant community transitions were tied mostly to climate in the mountain steppe, to grazing intensity and climate in the steppe, and to neither in the desert steppe.

title: Rangeland degradation in Mongolia: A systematic review of the evidence
data_and_method: Systematic review of 114 studies
finding: Reviews 114 studies from 1950 to 2021: 80 used field data, 21 remote sensing alone and 8 both, and 66 named grazing as the only driver. There is no standard definition of degradation. Nationwide estimates of the degraded share range from 22% to 95% depending on method (Table 1).
note: Searched Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar and Mongolian and Russian sources, with one screener. Recommends combining remote sensing with long-term field monitoring. Open copy at par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10381573.

title: Grazing Effects on Mongolian Steppe Vegetation—A Systematic Review of Local Literature
data_and_method: Systematic review of 44 Mongolian-language publications covering 109 sites
finding: Heavy grazing reduced cover, richness and biomass in desert, dry and high mountain steppe, with little or even positive effect in meadow and mountain steppe.
note: Shows what the Mongolian-language literature adds.

title: Changing Climate and Overgrazing Are Decimating Mongolian Steppes
data_and_method: Merged passive-microwave vegetation optical depth at 0.25 degrees; per-cell regression on precipitation and temperature over 1-8 month windows with 0-7 month leads, keeping the best fit
finding: Climate-predicted optical depth accounts for about 60% of the decline (ratio of trend slopes), over 80% in the west and south-east. Residual declines match goat increases in central Mongolia and fires in the east by spatial pattern.
note: Applied to NDVI, the same residual method found no significant trends. Choosing the best of many climate windows per cell favours the climate share. The goat and fire attribution rests on pattern matching.

title: Satellite observed widespread decline in Mongolian grasslands largely due to overgrazing
data_and_method: MODIS Aqua NDVI at 1 km with MAIAC correction and harmonic time-series fits; province-level livestock statistics; 64 weather stations
finding: Mean NDVI fell about 12% between 2002 and 2012, most at the southern edge of the grassland. Across provinces, NDVI decline correlated with cumulative herd increase (r2 0.85 for grassland, 0.74 for sparse vegetation) and with summer precipitation (r2 0.30).
note: The widely quoted 80% is this cross-province r2, not a decomposition of the decline. The record starts after the 1999-2002 dzuds, so part of the herd increase is recovery. Open copy at NASA NTRS.

title: Differentiating anthropogenic modification and precipitation-driven change on vegetation productivity on the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Rainfall-adjusted residual trends of MODIS and AVHRR vegetation indices, by administrative unit
finding: After adjusting for rainfall, vegetation trends were negatively related to livestock density in Mongolia (R2 0.59 for EVI) and positively related to population density in Inner Mongolia.

title: Satellite-indicated long-term vegetation changes and their drivers on the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: NDVI trends and phenology against temperature and precipitation
finding: NDVI rose until 1998 and then stalled, leaving no significant trend over the full period. Precipitation was the dominant factor for steppe. Notes that satellite greening and ground-observed production declines disagree.

title: NDVI-Based Long-Term Vegetation Dynamics and Its Response to Climatic Change in the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: AVHRR GIMMS and MODIS NDVI, cross-calibrated
finding: NDVI rose until the mid or late 1990s and fell afterwards as precipitation dropped. The decline of the 2000s is attributed mostly to a hotter and drier climate.

title: Spatial and Temporal Characteristics of Vegetation NDVI Changes and the Driving Forces in Mongolia during 1982–2015
data_and_method: NDVI with Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall and the geographical detector
finding: Degraded and improved areas were roughly equal. Desert steppe and Gobi degraded while meadow and alpine steppe improved. Change in livestock numbers was the dominant factor for most vegetation types.

title: Grassland greening on the Mongolian Plateau despite higher grazing intensity
data_and_method: GIMMS NDVI3g at county level (199 Mongolian soums, 60 Inner Mongolian counties); CRU climate; livestock as animal units per km2 of grassland; spatial Durbin panel model with fixed effects
finding: Growing-season NDVI rose 0.005 per decade in Mongolia and 0.014 in Inner Mongolia. In Mongolia, 100 mm more rain raised NDVI 6.0% and 1 C of warming lowered it 1.2%. Animal density had a small positive elasticity (0.09) that was still the largest standardized effect.
note: County averages and the assumption that all animals graze may hide local overgrazing. Purevjav et al. 2025 show that correlational herd estimates can differ in sign from causal ones; fixed effects, which this study uses, narrow but do not close the gap. Karnieli et al. 2013 show how grazed land can look greener.

title: Divergent processes and trends of desertification in Inner Mongolia and Mongolia
data_and_method: MODIS vegetation cover grades; general linear model
finding: Desert extent fell by over 7% (about 11% in Inner Mongolia and 5% in Mongolia). Rising precipitation and temperature explain over 75% of the change.

title: Impact of human activities and climate change on the grassland dynamics under different regime policies in the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Grassland NPP and land cover change
finding: Grassland NPP rose 17.9% in Mongolia and 30.5% in Inner Mongolia. Grassland degraded on 18.6% of area in Mongolia and 9.8% in Inner Mongolia, mainly from human activity.

title: Distinguishing the vegetation dynamics induced by anthropogenic factors using vegetation optical depth and AVHRR NDVI: A cross-border study on the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Residual trends of vegetation optical depth and AVHRR NDVI
finding: Mongolia's grasslands showed a human-induced decline in aboveground biomass linked to livestock growth, with no matching decline in canopy greenness.
note: Biomass and greenness disagree, so the choice of index changes the conclusion.

title: Synergistic effects of climate change and grazing on net primary production of Mongolian grasslands
data_and_method: Process-based ecosystem model (DLEM) with a grazing module
finding: Growing-season precipitation and temperature explain 65% and 45% of interannual variation in aboveground production. Historical grazing reduced it by 2-15.4%. Dry sites sustain about half the grazing intensity of wet sites.

title: Risk and vulnerability of Mongolian grasslands under climate change
data_and_method: Probabilistic drought risk with a process-based vegetation model at 0.5 degrees
finding: Hazardous droughts became more frequent in 1996-2015. Drought risk to productivity rose about 10%, mainly from climate. Grazing intensity was 34% higher than in 1976-1995.

title: Climate rather than overgrazing explains most rangeland primary productivity change in Mongolia
data_and_method: Soum-level December livestock census (1984-2023) and June herd surveys (2016-2024); Landsat and MODIS NDVI on summer grazing ranges, checked against ground biomass; ERA5-Land weather; two-stage instrumental-variable design using winter-range dzud and herd size
finding: Doubling herd size lowers summer NDVI by about 4% in the short run, with effects in mountain taiga, forest steppe and steppe and none in semi-desert and desert. Over 10-year differences the herd effect disappears. Weather explains 38% of variation year to year and climate 45% over decades, against under 2% and under 10% for herd size.
note: The outcome is NDVI as a productivity proxy, and the authors call for other attributes of rangeland health. Regressions without fixed effects gave a positive herd effect; adding fixed effects brought estimates closer to the causal ones overall, less so by zone. Data and code on Dryad (doi:10.5061/dryad.bg79cnpmz).

title: No Signs of Long-term Greening Trend in Western Mongolian Grasslands
region: Western Mongolia: Mongolian Altai and western Khangai
data_and_method: GIMMS NDVI3g monthly maxima (1982-2010) for two forest-steppe regions; larch tree-ring chronologies used to reconstruct March-June NDVI back to 1940
finding: The satellite record began in the 1980-82 drought and ran into a wet 1990s, which produces a linear greening trend. The reconstruction shows no long-term trend from 1940 to 2010. July drought index declined from 1970 to 2018.
note: Forest steppe only, spring and early summer only, and the reconstruction was not tested on held-out years. A warning about trends fitted to records that start in the 1980s.

title: Revealing the dual impacts of climate change and grazing on vegetation in Mongolia: Permafrost buffering and the paradox of greening
data_and_method: July NDVI against climate variables and livestock density, with vegetation memory
finding: NDVI rose significantly. Contributions were precipitation 53.1%, temperature 33.9% and livestock density 4.0%. The authors state that NDVI greening or stability masked actual rangeland degradation.

title: Spatiotemporal variability in drivers of grassland degradation and recovery under economic transformation in Mongolia
data_and_method: NDVI, LAI and NPP combined; Bayesian belief network; downscaled gridded livestock
finding: Grasslands shifted from non-significant degradation to non-significant recovery. Precipitation, evapotranspiration and temperature were the main drivers, with a combined contribution of 67-75%.

title: Assessment of vegetation change on the Mongolian Plateau over three decades using different remote sensing products
data_and_method: Five satellite indices compared (GPP, NPP, NDVI, LAI, fractional cover)
finding: GPP, NPP and NDVI trend upward while LAI and fractional cover trend downward. Only 3.4% of the plateau shows consistent trends across indices.
note: Direct evidence that the answer depends on the index chosen.

title: Revisiting vegetation activity of Mongolian Plateau using multiple remote sensing datasets
data_and_method: GPP, solar-induced fluorescence and NDVI against environmental factors
finding: Summer vegetation activity was mostly increasing or stable. It correlates positively with temperature and negatively with vapour pressure deficit.

title: Impacts of climate change and human activities on vegetation dynamics on the Mongolian Plateau, East Asia from 2000 to 2023
data_and_method: MODIS kNDVI; Theil-Sen, Mann-Kendall, residual analysis
finding: kNDVI increased overall, more in the south than in the north. Climate dominated change on about 51% of the plateau and inhibited growth in the north.

title: Analyzing vegetation dynamic trend on the Mongolian Plateau based on the Hurst exponent and influencing factors from 1982–2013
data_and_method: GIMMS NDVI3g trends; Hurst exponent
finding: NDVI rose slightly, mainly in the south of the plateau. Hurst analysis predicts improvement over a larger area than degradation. Precipitation is the dominant factor.
note: The Hurst exponent measures persistence of the past trend. It is not a tested forecast.

title: Are Mongolian rangelands overgrazed? Estimating grassland utilisation and sustainable stocking rates with a vegetation model
data_and_method: LPJ-GUESS with one C3 grass type and a daily livestock module at 0.1° (about 9 km), driven by ERA5-Land and soum livestock counts in sheep units; human appropriation of net primary production; potential livestock density as the largest herd that never exhausts forage within a decade; checked against GOSIF GPP, MODIS NPP and a field-calibrated biomass map of the eastern steppe
finding: Livestock reduced NPP and peak biomass by 9% on average over 1970-2023 and by 18% in 2018. Human appropriation of production rose from 6% in 1970 to 21% in 2018 and was highest in the desert. Potential density was 1.3 to 1.8 sheep units per hectare, lowest in the 2000s when rainfall fell. Reported herds exceeded it on 33% of grazing land in 2019, mostly in desert and desert steppe and around settlements.
note: Read in full. Agreement with satellite products is moderate (R² 0.44 to 0.56). The model overestimates NPP by about 36% on average against MODIS and underestimates it in the desert. The authors say the 33% may be too high, since 44% of the overstocked cells are desert with no MODIS NPP to check against and 40% have NPP underestimated. The close match with other carrying capacity methods is largely built in, as all were computed from the same simulated biomass. No selective grazing, herder mobility or wildlife. Model and code on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17465156, the version the paper cites).

title: Spatio-Temporal Variations in Grassland Carrying Capacity Derived from Remote Sensing NPP in Mongolia
data_and_method: GLASS and MODIS NPP converted to biomass; carrying capacity
finding: MODIS shows biomass rising from 2000 to 2020 while GLASS shows it falling from 1982 to 2018. 37.5% of grassland is severely overgrazed and 31.9-40.7% within sustainable limits. The east can support current herds.
note: Another case of two products disagreeing on the trend.

title: Beyond Climate and Grazing: Impact of Herder Mobility on Steppe Vegetation
data_and_method: 275 vegetation plots (10 × 10 m, cover by species) at 11 sites near settlements or in open steppe, interviews with 249 herder households on their 2019 moves, topsoil samples; variation partitioning, mixed models and indicator species
finding: The four predictor groups explain 34% of plant composition. Climate alone explains 11%, disturbance 7%, mobility 6% and soil 4%, with large overlaps. More moves between seasonal pastures go with higher richness and more palatable species. Cover and palatable cover rise with distance from settlements, clearly so only where warm-season rain is below 165 mm. Dysphania aristata, Artemisia adamsii and Leymus chinensis indicate heavy disturbance.
note: Read in full. Mobility enters as a site average, so its effect rests on 10 sites, and p-values are not corrected for multiple tests. Plot data on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.18936374), a possible check for a map of palatable cover.

title: Sensitivity of Vegetation Greenness to Multi-Depth Soil Moisture on the Mongolian Plateau: Nonlinear Responses Revealed by RF–SHAP
data_and_method: NDVI with ERA5-Land multi-layer soil moisture; random forest with SHAP
finding: NDVI is most sensitive to soil moisture at 7-28 cm, then 0-7 cm, then 28-100 cm, with nonlinear threshold responses.

title: Grazing impacts on Mongolian grasslands assessed by an eco-hydrology model
data_and_method: Process-based eco-hydrology model (NICE-INVERSE)
finding: Livestock water use is 100-120 million m3 per year, the same order as mining and urban use, with large regional variation in per-animal use.

title: One Border, Two Steppes: Comparative Rangeland Quality in Mongolia and China
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Cross-border comparison of rangeland quality, per title. SSRN blocks automated access.

title: Regionalized grazing–productivity associations and livestock-specific breakpoint candidates across Mongolia’s dryland rangelands
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Grazing-productivity breakpoints by region, per title.

title: National report on the rangeland health of Mongolia: Second assessment
venue: Green Gold-Animal Health Project, SDC, Ulaanbaatar
data_and_method: 1,516 NAMEM sites measured yearly since 2011 with line-point intercept, gap intercept and clipped biomass; ecological site groups and state-and-transition models assign degradation levels and recovery classes
finding: In 2016, 42.4% of sites were non-degraded, 13.5% slightly, 21.1% moderately, 12.8% heavily and 10.3% fully degraded. Heavy and full degradation rose 5.9 and 4.3 points from 2014. Recovery classes were 43% I, 29% II, 16% III and 12% IV, with none in V.
note: Chapters 1-3 read. The report contradicts itself on the 2014 comparison: chapter 3 says altered sites fell 8 points, while the summary, and the 48% figure for 2014 in Sainnemekh et al. 2022, show an increase. A photo-point system covers a further 4,200 sites in 278 soums. A third assessment appears to exist (gazar.gov.mn).

title: Trend analysis of MODIS NDVI time series for detecting land degradation and regeneration in Mongolia
data_and_method: MODIS NDVI trend analysis with land cover and meteorological data
finding: Eleven years of data gave statistically significant trends for 50% of Mongolia. The method detected deforestation, fire, mining, urban expansion and grassland regeneration, and large trend areas followed precipitation change.

title: Tracking desertification on the Mongolian steppe through NDVI and field-survey data
data_and_method: Line transects with NDVI
finding: Plant density fell 16%, but continued annual fluctuation indicates that irreversible change had not occurred. Cover was greater near water points.

title: Contraction of the Gobi Desert, 2000–2012
data_and_method: Satellite vegetation data with the aridity index
finding: The Gobi contracted over the period, driven mainly by precipitation. Notes that the desert boundary is poorly defined.

title: Monitoring desertification in Mongolia based on Landsat images and Google Earth Engine from 1990 to 2020
data_and_method: Landsat composites for seven dates from 1990 to 2020 in Earth Engine; MSAVI, albedo, topsoil grain size index and six bands; six classifiers trained on 1,000 points labelled from 2019-2020 field quadrats and Google Earth imagery, with a random 70/30 split; random forest importance and trend comparison for drivers
finding: Maximum entropy classified best, with 96% accuracy and kappa 0.94. Desertified land grew from 1990 to 2005 and shrank afterwards, for an overall gain of about 1,900 km² a year. The light and moderate classes changed most, mainly in the east, while the severe classes changed little. Precipitation ranked first and livestock low, and the 2005 turn matches a break in the rainfall trend.
note: Read in full. The classes are defined by vegetation cover, so the naturally sparse Gobi counts as extremely severe desertification. Accuracy is reported once, from a random split of points labelled in 2019 and 2020, and not for the earlier maps. The driver ranking explains where cover is low, which largely restates the rainfall gradient. No data availability statement.

title: Spatio-Temporal Pattern of Land Degradation from 1990 to 2015 in Mongolia
data_and_method: 30 m land cover maps for 1990, 2010 and 2015
finding: Land change over the 25 years was dominated by degradation, with restoration in some areas and improving restoration capacity.

title: Desertification Information Extraction Based on Feature Space Combinations on the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Landsat 8; Albedo-NDVI, Albedo-MSAVI and Albedo-TGSI feature spaces
finding: Overall accuracies were 84.5%, 85.6% and 88.3%. The best index pair depends on vegetation cover, with Albedo-TGSI best for very sparse cover.

title: Assessment of land cover change and desertification using remote sensing technology in a local region of Mongolia
finding: Abstract not read yet.

title: Assessing environmentally sensitive land to desertification using MEDALUS method in Mongolia
data_and_method: Modified MEDALUS sensitivity index with nine factors
finding: The area in the highest sensitivity class increased about five times between 2003 and 2008.
note: Compares two single years.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of desertification on the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: 30 m Landsat in Google Earth Engine; feature space and five machine learning models
finding: 2010 marked a turn from degradation to restoration on the plateau. From 2010 to 2020 desertified land kept deteriorating in southern Mongolia while Inner Mongolia recovered. Best model accuracy was 88.2%.

title: Assessment of Land Desertification and Its Drivers on the Mongolian Plateau Using Intensity Analysis and the Geographical Detector Technique
region: Border area: East Ujimqin Banner and three Mongolian soums
data_and_method: Visual interpretation; intensity analysis; geographical detector
finding: Desertification on the Mongolian side concentrated in Matad soum and was driven mostly by natural conditions.

title: Mapping Vegetation Changes in Mongolian Grasslands (1990–2024) Using Landsat Data and Advanced Machine Learning Algorithm
data_and_method: Landsat with XGBoost classification
finding: Montane grassland declined 6.2% while other grassland types increased. Reported overall accuracy is above 94%.

title: Spatial–Temporal and Driving Factors of Land Use/Cover Change in Mongolia from 1990 to 2021
data_and_method: Annual Landsat land cover with random forest
finding: 17.6% of land changed class at least once. Barren land increased while grassland and forest decreased.

title: Updatable dataset revealing decade changes in land cover types in Mongolia
data_and_method: Object-based 30 m land cover in 11 classes
finding: Barren land shows an overall decrease over 30 years, real steppe a decrease and desert steppe an increase. Accuracies are 82-92%.
note: Hao et al. 2023 report barren land increasing over a similar period.

title: Sandstorms and desertification in Mongolia, an example of future climate events: a review
data_and_method: Review
finding: Reviews the 2021 sandstorms and their background. Cites a 2.24 C rise in annual mean temperature from 1940 to 2015, a 7% fall in precipitation, and more than three quarters of land affected by drought and desertification.

title: Research Progress of Desertification and Its Prevention in Mongolia
data_and_method: Literature review
finding: Finds that monitoring has been low-resolution and delayed, that driver contributions have not been quantified by region, and that desertification models for Mongolia are underdeveloped.

title: Spatial assessment of soil wind erosion using WEQ approach in Mongolia
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Wind erosion assessment with the WEQ approach, per title.

title: Ecological vulnerability assessment of typical grasslands on the Mongolian Plateau: Abrupt change detection and driving mechanism analysis
data_and_method: Sensitivity-resilience-pressure index with spatial PCA; abrupt change detection
finding: Vulnerability declined slowly overall, with an abrupt change in 2014 after which the degraded area expanded about 57.6%, mainly in the south and north-east. Natural factors were the main drivers.

title: Change Patterns of Ecological Vulnerability and Its Dominant Factors in Mongolia During 2000–2022
data_and_method: MODIS ecological vulnerability index; geographical detector
finding: Vulnerability is moderate on average and its centre is shifting south-west. Maximum temperature is the leading driver overall, with precipitation leading in the east, centre and south.

title: Desertification and land degradation problems in soums in different natural regions of Mongolia
venue: Mongolian Journal of Geography and Geoecology
data_and_method: Remote sensing, ground observations and socio-economic indicators
finding: Describes land cover change linked to drought and degradation in a forest-steppe, a dry-steppe and a desert-steppe soum. Quotes 77.8% of territory showing degradation.
note: From the institute that runs the national assessments.

title: Abrupt shift to hotter and drier climate over inner East Asia beyond the tipping point
data_and_method: Tree-ring reconstructions of heatwaves and soil moisture
finding: Heatwave and drought concurrence over the last two decades is unprecedented in 260 years. Soil moisture deficit and surface warming reinforce each other, and the shift may be irreversible.

title: Past and future drought in Mongolia
data_and_method: Tree-ring drought reconstruction with climate model ensembles
finding: The 2000s drought was highly unusual but not unprecedented in two millennia. The model ensemble suggests drying until mid-century and a reversal afterwards as precipitation rises.

title: Assessment of drought frequency, duration, and severity and its impact on pasture production in Mongolia
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Drought frequency and its effect on pasture production, per title.

title: Climate Impact on the Seasonal and Interannual Variation in NDVI and GPP in Mongolia
data_and_method: ERA5-Land with NDVI and GPP
finding: Annual temperature rose 0.94 C and precipitation 32 mm (about 13%), mainly in the north and east. Maximum NDVI rose 0.025 per decade and GPP 38%, with no change or slight decline in the central steppe in May-June.

title: Rapid loss of lakes on the Mongolian Plateau
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
data_and_method: Landsat lake survey with ground census
finding: Lakes larger than 1 km2 fell from 785 to 577, a loss of 17.6% in Mongolia and 34.0% in Inner Mongolia. In Mongolia precipitation was the dominant driver.

title: Decreased river runoff on the Mongolian Plateau since around 2000
data_and_method: Runoff records for 30 rivers; Budyko framework; comparison with CMIP6
finding: Runoff dropped abruptly around 2000 in 21 of 30 rivers, mainly from precipitation change. CMIP6 simulations did not reproduce the drop.
note: A caution for using CMIP6 output as forecast input in this region.

title: Analysis of dust storms observed in Mongolia during 1937–1999
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Station record of dust storms, per title.

title: Sources of Asian dust and role of climate change versus desertification in Asian dust emission
data_and_method: Dust emission and transport model with station data
finding: Deserts in Mongolia and in western and northern China contribute about 70% of Asian dust emissions. Meteorology and climate influenced emissions more than desertification did.

title: Why super sandstorm 2021 in North China?
data_and_method: Reanalysis and CMIP6 large ensemble
finding: Attributes the March 2021 sandstorm to dry, loose ground in the Mongolian source area after temperature swings and low precipitation, combined with a very strong Mongolian cyclone.

title: Dust Intensity Across Vegetation Types in Mongolia: Drivers and Trends
data_and_method: Station dust intensity with reanalysis, satellite and statistical data
finding: Dust intensity rose at about two thirds of stations. The authors attribute most of it to anthropogenic factors, except in alpine meadow.
note: Drivers are GDP and population statistics, which are coarse proxies.

title: Dzuds, droughts, and livestock mortality in Mongolia
data_and_method: Livestock mortality against climate variables
finding: Mortality is tied most strongly to winter temperature, with prior summer drought as a trigger. The climate-only model explains 48.4% of mortality variability.

title: Cross-boundary and cross-level dynamics increase vulnerability to severe winter disasters (dzud) in Mongolia
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Vulnerability to dzud, per title.

title: Cold-season disasters on the Eurasian steppes: Climate-driven or man-made
data_and_method: Multiple regression by province on hazards and socioeconomic data
finding: Combined hazards (drought, cold, snow) and herder vulnerability explain 93.5% of dzud mortality in roughly equal parts (47.3% and 46.2%).

title: Migration under economic transition and changing climate in Mongolia
data_and_method: National labour survey data
finding: Over 80% of migration was to cities, mostly Ulaanbaatar. Migration rates rose after the 2009-2010 dzud.

title: Rangeland Degradation, Vegetation Dynamics, and Household Income in a Mongolian Pastoral System: Panel Evidence from Öndörshireet Soum
data_and_method: Sentinel-2 NDVI, 120 soil plots and a 114-household panel
finding: Nearly 90% of plots were at least moderately degraded and NDVI declined. Household income is positively associated with vegetation condition.

title: Exploring linked ecological and cultural tipping points in Mongolia
data_and_method: Review with regional analysis of climate, livestock and remote sensing data
finding: A large share of rangeland is altered from its potential, but few areas have crossed an irreversible threshold. Khangai, northern and central regions may approach a tipping point if grazing pressure is not reduced.

title: Prospects for the sustainability of social-ecological systems (SES) on the Mongolian plateau: five critical issues
data_and_method: Synthesis from an expert workshop
finding: Identifies five critical issues, among them the unsustainability of large-scale afforestation in arid and semi-arid Inner Mongolia, and warns that lessons from Inner Mongolia may not transfer to Mongolia.

title: Theoretical Approaches and Practical Assessment of Socio-Economic Effects of Desertification in Mongolia
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
data_and_method: Household questionnaire surveys
finding: Surveys record growing effects of desertification on herding, water supply and living standards across natural zones.

title: A Review of the Socio-Economic Impacts of Desertification and Land Degradation in Mongolia
venue: Mongolian Journal of Geography and Geoecology
data_and_method: Review of 25 reports and articles
finding: Repeats the figure of 76.9% of territory affected, with 23.3% severe or very severe. Reports 665,058 people moving to Ulaanbaatar from 2000 to 2023 and losses of 1.2 trillion MNT per year.
note: Secondary source. Abstract, selected passages and reference list read. Trace each figure to the ministry reports it cites.

title: Impact of the Dzud Disaster on Nomadic Livestock Farming in Mongolia
data_and_method: Household survey, carrying capacity analysis and economic assessment
finding: 63.3% of surveyed households lost livestock in the 2023-2024 dzud. Total damage including lost ecosystem services is estimated at 1.5-1.9 billion USD. Overgrazing is identified as a key vulnerability.

title: Snow Cover Inversion Driven by Dzud Events in Mongolia from 2000 to 2024
data_and_method: MODIS snow index checked against Sentinel-2
finding: Maps snow cover during the five most severe dzud events. Snow cover shows a slight decline over 25 years with large year-to-year swings.

title: Applying Multi-Sensor Satellite Data to Identify Key Natural Factors in Annual Livestock Change and Winter Livestock Disaster (Dzud) in Mongolian Nomadic Pasturelands
data_and_method: Multi-sensor satellite drivers; PCA, stepwise regression and random forest
finding: Random forest explained annual livestock change with R2 above 0.9 in most soums. Summer and winter variables were about equally important, and the main drivers differ by region.

title: Impacts of climate hazards on livestock populations in the Eurasian dryland countries
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Climate hazards and livestock populations, per title.

title: Increasing dust storms in Mongolia and its association with natural and anthropogenic factors
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Increasing dust storms and their drivers, per title.

title: Lessons from the Dzud: Community-Based Rangeland Management Increases the Adaptive Capacity of Mongolian Herders to Winter Disasters
data_and_method: Comparison of herder communities with and without formal community-based management
finding: Herders in formal groups showed greater adaptive capacity, through knowledge exchange, information access and proactive behaviour.
note: Read from the RePEc summary.

title: Do pasture user groups lead to improved rangeland condition in the Mongolian Gobi Desert?
data_and_method: Pasture user group areas of three and twelve years compared with non-group areas; interviews and field indicators
finding: Some indicators differed between group and non-group areas, but no group-specific institutions or activities explained the difference. Concludes the effect of groups on rangeland condition may be overstated.

title: Social Outcomes of Community-based Rangeland Management in Mongolian Steppe Ecosystems
data_and_method: 77 formal groups compared with 65 traditional neighbourhoods
finding: Group members were more proactive and used more management practices. Most livelihood measures did not differ.

title: Policies and Regulations for Desertification Prevention and Control in Mongolia
data_and_method: Policy and legal review
finding: Reviews Mongolia's desertification policies and regulations and argues for a dedicated desertification prevention and control law and a joint mechanism with China.

title: Context matters: Rethinking resource governance theories for Mongolian pastoral systems
data_and_method: Survey of 760 households
finding: Rules, social capital and forage availability predict whether a household reserves pasture. Social ties and environmental conditions predict mobility.

title: Implementing a resilience-based management system in Mongolia's rangelands
data_and_method: Description of a national programme
finding: Describes the national system built on ecological site models, standardized monitoring by government agencies, rangeland use agreements with pasture user groups, and product traceability. Ecological outcomes still need assessment.

title: Optimal Irrigation Regime for Woody Species Potentially Suitable for Effective and Sustainable Afforestation in the Desert Region of Mongolia
data_and_method: Irrigation trial with four woody species
finding: The lowest irrigation regime was optimal for three of four species. The highest regime grew trees faster with lower survival.
note: Shows the irrigation that afforestation in the desert zone involves.

title: Comparison of water use efficiency and biomass production in 10-year-oldPopulus sibiricaandUlmus pumilaplantations in Lun soum, Mongolia
data_and_method: Ten-year-old stands in the Korea-Mongolia Green Belt plantation
finding: Ulmus pumila had higher water use efficiency than Populus sibirica, which produced about 2.5 times more biomass.

title: A way forward to sustainable international forestry cooperation: a case study of the 'Greenbelt Plantation Project in Mongolia'
data_and_method: Mid-term project assessment
finding: Assesses the Korea-Mongolia Greenbelt Plantation project with a focus on project sustainability and government participation.

title: Estimation of the Carrying Capacity and Relative Stocking Density of Mongolian grasslands under various adaptation scenarios
data_and_method: Ecological model with socio-economic data, validated with NAMEM data
finding: Carrying capacity ranges from 2.8 sheep units per hectare in the north to 0.3 in parts of the Gobi. Relative stocking density averages 1.07 and is highest near Ulaanbaatar.

title: The effectiveness of forecast-based humanitarian assistance in anticipation of extreme winters: a case study of vulnerable herders in Mongolia
data_and_method: Quasi-experimental evaluation of forecast-based cash and veterinary kits
finding: Found reduced mortality and higher offspring survival for some species, and that early timing matters.
note: Shows that forecasts have an operational use and that their effect can be evaluated.

title: State Policy and Pasture Degradation in Inner Asia
data_and_method: Comparative research project
finding: Areas that kept mobile pastoralism, such as Mongolia, reported much less pasture degradation than areas that moved to static, mechanised systems.

title: Climate adaptation, local institutions, and rural livelihoods: A comparative study of herder communities in Mongolia and Inner Mongolia, China
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Comparative study of herder communities, per title.

title: The Degradation of Rangelands in Mongolia: An Actor-Centered Institutionalist Approach
data_and_method: Policy documents and semi-structured interviews; actor-centred institutionalism
finding: Explains why a Rangeland Law has not been adopted over decades: institutional factors and political interests outweigh actor-level factors.
note: States that 65% of rangelands are degraded to some extent relative to reference.

title: Has the Three Norths Forest Shelterbelt Program solved the desertification and dust storm problems in arid and semiarid China?
data_and_method: Assessment with afforestation, desertification and dust storm data
finding: Finds little solid evidence that the Three Norths shelterbelt afforestation controlled desertification and dust storms, and concludes its importance has been overstated.

title: Excessive reliance on afforestation in China's arid and semi-arid regions: Lessons in ecological restoration
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Lessons from afforestation in arid and semi-arid China, per title.

title: Contributions of ecological programs to vegetation restoration in arid and semiarid China
data_and_method: Vegetation indices, land use and climate factors
finding: Climate and CO2 contributed more than 50% (1982-2000) and 70% (2001-2015) to vegetation restoration. Ecological programmes contributed about 20%.

title: Vegetation restoration in Northern China: A contrasted picture
data_and_method: GIMMS NDVI fractional cover with rainfall and forestry statistics
finding: Vegetation cover rose across the region. The authors infer a role for restoration in the east and centre and report low survival of planted trees.

title: Severe depletion of soil moisture following land-use changes for ecological restoration: Evidence from northern China
data_and_method: Synthesis of 1,740 observations at 83 sites
finding: Afforestation significantly depleted soil moisture, while natural restoration did not. Planting is judged practical only above about 600 mm annual precipitation.
note: Munkhzul et al. 2021 report 120-370 mm across Mongolian steppe sites.

title: Land use and land cover change in Inner Mongolia - understanding the effects of China's re-vegetation programs
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Effects of China's re-vegetation programmes on land cover, per title.

title: Discrimination between climate and human-induced dryland degradation
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Origin of the residual trend approach, per title.

title: Can human-induced land degradation be distinguished from the effects of rainfall variability? A case study in South Africa
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Separating human-induced degradation from rainfall variability, per title.

title: Limits to detectability of land degradation by trend analysis of vegetation index data
data_and_method: Losses of 10 to 40% inserted at different rates and start years into 16 seasons of 1 km AVHRR NDVI from a protected savanna; linear, Mann-Kendall and residual trend tests
finding: With the rainfall-driven positive trend present, seasonal NDVI had to fall 30-40% before significant negative trends appeared, while degraded land nearby is only 10-20% below intact land. Without that trend, a 20% loss was detectable. Losses near the start or end of the series went undetected. Residual trend analysis became unreliable at losses of 20% or more, because the loss weakens the NDVI-rainfall relation it relies on.
note: Read in full. The authors recommend testing a method on simulated losses before claiming it maps degradation, and stress that results depend on the start and end years. They say the limits differ by environment and have to be tested locally.

title: Detecting dryland degradation using Time Series Segmentation and Residual Trend analysis (TSS-RESTREND)
data_and_method: Residual trends combined with break detection (BFAST)
finding: Detected degradation in 5.25% of pixels against 2.0% for the residual trend method alone, and captured the timing and direction of change at two known sites.

title: The impact of dataset selection on land degradation assessment
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Effect of dataset choice on degradation assessment, per title.

title: Assessing Land Degradation and Desertification Using Vegetation Index Data: Current Frameworks and Future Directions
data_and_method: Review
finding: Reviews vegetation-index methods for degradation. Calls for robust, comparable validation and for detection of low-intensity degradation.

title: Challenges for remote sensing of the Sustainable Development Goal SDG 15.3.1 productivity indicator
data_and_method: Review
finding: Argues that vegetation indices alone are not an adequate SDG 15.3.1 productivity indicator. Names four gaps, including the lack of reference conditions and the difficulty of separating human from natural causes.

title: Developing good practice guidance for estimating land degradation in the context of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Good practice guidance for SDG 15.3.1, per title.

title: Remote sensing of dryland ecosystem structure and function: Progress, challenges, and opportunities
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Review of dryland remote sensing, per title.

title: The use of remote sensing for desertification studies: A review
data_and_method: Review of studies since 1991
finding: Landsat is the main data source, classification and change detection are the main methods, and China has the most studies.

title: Do vegetation indices provide a reliable indication of vegetation degradation? A case study in the Mongolian pastures
region: Mongolia: mountain steppe and steppe along the Trans-Mongolian Railway
data_and_method: Six fence-line pairs (railway fenced since the 1950s); Landsat 7 EVI; field density, biomass and cover; leaf spectra
finding: Ungrazed plots had higher density (27 vs 18 plants per m2), biomass (129 vs 59 g/m2) and cover (66% vs 52%), yet lower EVI (0.22 vs 0.28). Unpalatable species with high near-infrared reflectance dominate grazed plots, while palatable grasses yellow by mid-summer.
note: Six pairs, no desert steppe, late-season images. The season of measurement may drive the sign of the effect.

title: Grassland canopy cover and aboveground biomass in Mongolia and Inner Mongolia: Spatiotemporal estimates and controlling factors
data_and_method: More than 1,000 field samples; rule-based regression trees on MODIS
finding: Models of canopy cover and aboveground biomass reached validation R2 of 0.67 and 0.68.

title: Mapping pasture biomass in Mongolia using Partial Least Squares, Random Forest regression and Landsat 8 imagery
data_and_method: 553 field sites; Landsat 8; random forest and partial least squares
finding: Both models reached R2 of about 0.75 for pasture biomass, mapped at 30 m.

title: Estimating fractional vegetation cover and aboveground biomass for land degradation assessment in eastern Mongolia steppe: combining ground vegetation data and remote sensing
data_and_method: 256 plots from the national pasture-monitoring database; Sentinel-2; random forest
finding: R2 was 0.81 for fractional cover and 0.76 for biomass. Landsat NDVI decreased significantly on 58% of the area.
note: Uses the national monitoring database as ground truth.

title: Improving Landsat predictions of rangeland fractional cover with multitask learning and uncertainty
data_and_method: Temporal convolutional network on Landsat 5, 7 and 8 reflectance, NDVI and NBR2 in 64-day steps over two years, plus coordinates; trained on 52,012 line-point intercept plots from 2004-2019; tested on 5,780 plots held out at random by state and on five independent datasets; uncertainty from dropout at prediction time
finding: Yearly 30 m cover of annual and perennial forbs and grasses, shrubs, trees, litter and bare ground for western US rangelands, 1984-2019. Held-out plots gave 6.3% mean absolute error and 9.6% RMSE, with r² of 0.57 to 0.77 for most groups. On the independent datasets absolute errors were similar but r² was often lower, down to 0.08.
note: Read in full. Template for a field-trained condition map. Plots were held out at random rather than by region or year, and the maps before 2004 have no field check. Mongolia's network has 1,516 sites against 57,792 plots here, and it uses the same family of field methods (line-point intercept, a DIMA database). Maps on the Rangeland Analysis Platform.

title: Pasture condition in the Mongolian steppe: Cross-validating traditional ecological knowledge and field-based ecological surveys
data_and_method: 367 household interviews; field vegetation surveys; remote-sensing biomass
finding: Herders' assessments of pasture condition varied widely even within sites and had only a moderate association with field data, so field surveys are still needed.

title: Green is not always good: NDVI may not capture rangeland degradation in Mongolia
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Argues NDVI may not capture rangeland degradation, per title. SSRN blocks automated access.

title: Perception of Rangeland Degradation in Mongolia: The Role of Herder Groups and Local Ecological Knowledge
data_and_method: Herder surveys in a district with pasture user groups and one without; comparison with instrumental data
finding: Herders active in pasture user groups perceive more degradation, but the indicators they use do not differ. NDVI alone did not track the early-stage degradation herders report.

title: Greening–Function Decoupling and Land Degradation Risks in the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Index combining NDVI with NPP, evapotranspiration and land surface temperature
finding: Non-greening areas averaged 61.6%. Coordinated greening peaked at 33.2% (2016) and decoupled greening reached 19.6% (2012), so greening without functional improvement is common.

title: Can vegetation breakpoints in Eastern Mongolia rangeland be detected using Sentinel-1 coherence time series data?
data_and_method: Sentinel-1 coherence with optical and weather data; random forest breakpoint method compared with BFAST
finding: Random forest separated grazing-caused vegetation change from weather-caused change better than BFAST, detecting 44% of summer camp movements against 28%.

title: Evaluation of IMERG and ERA5 precipitation products over the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Evaluation of IMERG, ERA5 and ERA5-Land precipitation against gauges
finding: For daily precipitation ERA5-Land performed best, then ERA5, ERA-Interim and IMERG. All products overestimate weak and underestimate heavy rain, and perform worst in the sparse south-west.
note: Supports ERA5-Land as the rainfall input for Mongolia.

title: From Pixels to Mobile Pastoral Households: Scale Mismatch, Exposure Measurement, and Inference in Mongolian Rangeland Research
data_and_method: Methodological framework
finding: Sets out four mismatches between satellite pixels, grazing areas, administrative units and households, and argues that predictive agreement with a satellite productivity proxy does not establish household exposure or causality.
note: EarthArXiv preprint.

title: Above-ground biomass retrieval with multi-source data: Prediction and applicability analysis in Eastern Mongolia
data_and_method: Random forest on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2, with WorldView-2 and Landsat 8 also tested; validated against more than 600 field samples; dissimilarity index for the area where the model applies
finding: Sentinel-1 with Sentinel-2 gave the most accurate biomass estimates. The model applies to at least 72.61% of the steppe, and the areas outside are mostly at the grassland edges.
note: Found through the references of vanlaere2026, which reports R² 0.75 from cross-validation on 603 plots and uses the map for 2019-2021. A field-trained precedent from Mongolia.

title: Future Climate Impact on the Desertification in the Dry Land Asia Using AVHRR GIMMS NDVI3g Data
data_and_method: Regression of GIMMS NDVI3g on climate; CMIP5 ensemble under three RCPs
finding: Projects faster desertification under RCP8.5 across most of the Mongolian Plateau.
note: Extends a climate-NDVI regression into the future.

title: Assessment, driving mechanism identification and future scenario projection of desertification vulnerability in the Mongolian Plateau: an integrated study using multi-source data and machine learning
data_and_method: Improved MEDALUS index from 19 factors at 500 m, in five classes by natural breaks; XGBoost with SHAP to rank drivers; a convolutional network trained on 2000-2020 data with an 8:2 split, then fed CMIP6 inputs for 2040-2100
finding: Across the plateau, the very low and low classes grew by 55,320 and 94,249 km² over 2001-2020, and 73.5% of the area kept its class. Gains in Mongolia were smaller, and its very high class still covered more than 420,000 km². The bare soil index ranks as the top driver. Under SSP5-8.5 the very high class grows 8.4% by 2100.
note: Read in full. The driver model predicts the index from the 19 factors it is built from, the bare soil index among them, so its R² of 0.985 and its top driver are largely built in. The projection model was checked on a split of the same years. No test on later years or other regions is described, and no uncertainty range is given. The paper labels the low-emission scenario both SSP1-2.4 and SSP1-2.6 and describes the scenario numbers as degrees of warming, though they denote radiative forcing in W/m². The introduction applies Mongolia's 76.9% to the whole plateau. Page 15 contains text pasted from an AI chat interface. Data on request only.

title: Unveiling Drivers and Projecting Future Risks of Desertification Vulnerability in the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: MEDALUS with XGBoost; four SSPs
finding: High-vulnerability zones expanded over 2000-2020, and vulnerability intensifies under high-emission scenarios.
note: Same group as li2025vulnerability, which reports overall improvement for nearly the same period.

title: Projected distributions of Mongolian rangeland vegetation under future climate conditions
data_and_method: MaxEnt on 278 vegetation plots with downscaled CMIP6 climate
finding: Suitable habitat shrinks for desert steppe, steppe and meadow steppe under all scenarios, most for meadow steppe.

title: Projected Drought Risk to Vegetation Productivity Across the Mongolian Plateau Under CMIP6 Scenarios
data_and_method: Six CMIP6 models; SPEI; CASA NPP
finding: SPEI declines while NPP increases under all three scenarios. Drought probability rises markedly in 2061-2100.

title: Emergency constraint-based CMIP6 predictions for future droughts on the Mongolian Plateau
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Constrained CMIP6 drought projections, per title.

title: Prediction of Droughts in the Mongolian Plateau Based on the CMIP5 Model
data_and_method: CMIP5 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5; SPEI
finding: Drought increases under both scenarios and is projected to be more extreme in Mongolia than in Inner Mongolia.

title: Past dynamics and future prediction of the impacts of land use cover change and climate change on landscape ecological risk across the Mongolian plateau
data_and_method: Landscape loss index; random forest; FLUS land-use simulation under eight SSP-RCP scenarios
finding: The highest-risk zone expanded 30% since 2001. Higher emission scenarios enlarge high-risk areas.

title: Simulation and Prediction of Land Use/Cover Changes Based on CLUE-S and CA-Markov Models: A Case Study of a Typical Pastoral Area in Mongolia
data_and_method: CLUE-S and CA-Markov land-use models
finding: CLUE-S reproduced 2019 land cover better than CA-Markov. Projections favour the ecological protection scenario.
note: One of the few studies here that tests a model against a held-out year.

title: Historical and Future Changes in Extreme Climate Events and Their Effects on Vegetation on the Mongolian Plateau
data_and_method: Regression of NDVI on climate-extreme indices; three SSPs
finding: NDVI is projected to keep increasing to 2080, more slowly than in the historical period.

title: Urbanization and environmental policy effects on the future availability of grazing resources on the Mongolian Plateau: Modeling socio-environmental system dynamics
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: System dynamics model of future grazing resources, per title.

title: Assessment of potential soil erosion in Mongolia based on the RUSLE model and RCP 8.5 scenario
data_and_method: RUSLE soil erosion model under RCP8.5
finding: Area at very high or extreme erosion risk grows from 46,039 km2 to 48,961 km2 (2041-2060) and 51,769 km2 (2061-2080).

title: Estimation and Prediction of Grassland Cover in Western Mongolia Using MODIS-Derived Vegetation Indices
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Estimation and prediction of grassland cover from MODIS, per title.

title: A spatio-temporal prediction of NDVI based on precipitation: an application for grazing management in the arid and semi-arid grasslands
data_and_method: NARX and neural networks driven by precipitation
finding: Predicted spatio-temporal NDVI with a mean absolute percentage error of 11.6%.

title: Projections of desertification trends in Central Asia under global warming scenarios
data_and_method: CA-Markov with ISIMIP2b climate data
finding: Desert area has decreased while potential desert land increases under 1.5 and 2.0 C of warming.

title: Multi-scenario simulation of desertification in North China for 2030
data_and_method: Spatial system dynamics model; nine scenarios
finding: Temperature and rainfall are the most sensitive factors. Current programmes lead to reversal by 2030 under average climate.

title: EarthNet2021: A large-scale dataset and challenge for Earth surface forecasting as a guided video prediction task
venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
data_and_method: Benchmark dataset of 32,000 Sentinel-2 samples at 20 m with topography and weather
finding: Frames Earth surface forecasting as video prediction conditioned on future weather.

title: Multi-Modal Learning for Geospatial Vegetation Forecasting
venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
data_and_method: GreenEarthNet: 23,816 Sentinel-2 minicubes at 20 m (2017-2020) with E-OBS weather and elevation; Contextformer (vision transformer with a temporal transformer); tests on later years and new regions
finding: Forecasts 100 days of NDVI from 50 days of history with R2 0.62 and RMSE 0.14 (0.08 over the first 25 days), beating climatology (R2 0.58) on 66.8% of test cubes. Spatial context and weather both add skill.
note: Europe only. Uses observed future weather, which a real forecast would not have. Climatology was a baseline that older models failed to beat. Open preprint at arXiv:2303.16198.

title: Enhanced prediction of vegetation responses to extreme drought using deep learning and Earth observation data
data_and_method: ConvLSTM on Sentinel-2 with weather and topography
finding: Predicts surface reflectance from past weather and improves on benchmarks during extreme drought.

title: Forecasting vegetation indices from spatio-temporal remotely sensed data using deep learning-based approaches: A systematic literature review
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Systematic review of deep learning for vegetation index forecasting, per title.

title: Deep Learning for Vegetation Health Forecasting: A Case Study in Kenya
data_and_method: LSTM models on MODIS vegetation health
finding: Forecasts beat a persistence baseline and a shallow neural network.

title: Forecasting vegetation condition for drought early warning systems in pastoral communities in Kenya
data_and_method: Linear autoregression and Gaussian processes on MODIS and Landsat
finding: A drought alert based on the 3-month Vegetation Condition Index was predicted four weeks ahead with about 89% hit rate and 4% false alarms.
note: Simple models set a strong baseline at short horizons.

title: Identifying Dynamic Memory Effects on Vegetation State Using Recurrent Neural Networks
data_and_method: LSTM model of NDVI from climate and static variables
finding: Fits a global NDVI model to study memory effects, validated with spatio-temporal block cross-validation.

title: Deep learning projects future warming-induced vegetation growth changes under SSP scenarios
data_and_method: Deep learning models of climate-driven vegetation growth; SSP scenarios
finding: Projects little change under SSP1-1.9 and regional increases under SSP5-8.5.

title: Learning to forecast vegetation greenness at fine resolution over Africa with ConvLSTMs
data_and_method: ConvLSTM on Sentinel-2 NDVI guided by ERA5, SMAP and topography
finding: Forecasts the seasonal course of NDVI at fine resolution and the effect of weather anomalies better than baselines.

title: Predictability of abrupt shifts in dryland ecosystem functioning
data_and_method: Abrupt drops in rain-use efficiency detected with BFAST01 on GIMMS NDVI and CHIRPS; XGBoost on resilience, vegetation, rainfall, soil and human-pressure predictors; temporal cross-validation
finding: Predicted shifts one year ahead with 75.1% accuracy and 76.6% precision, with no significant loss up to three years and a drop from four. Rainfall variability, soil nitrogen, long-term rainfall trend, population density and NDVI variability mattered most. Autocorrelation alone missed many shifts.
note: A direct template for option B. Accuracy is on balanced classes, hyperparameters were tuned on a random split, and CHIRPS does not cover northern Mongolia. Data and code on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.10636821).

title: Future climate change risks and sustainable pathways for pastoralism in the eastern Eurasian drylands
data_and_method: Climate-rangeland-society model; three SSP climate scenarios and six socio-economic pathways
finding: Dzud risk intensifies from the mid-2030s under baseline pathways, with annual livestock mortality of 8-11 million sheep units, driven by compound hazards and persistent overstocking. Export-enhanced pathways reduce mortality.

title: Will the typical soums in the Selenge River Basin of Mongolia become more overgrazed in the future?
finding: Abstract not read yet.

title: Prediction of Sandstorm Moving Path in Mongolian Plateau Based on CNN-BiLSTM
data_and_method: CNN-BiLSTM on remote sensing and meteorological data
finding: Predicted sandstorm paths 1-24 hours ahead with accuracy, F1 and AUC above 0.80.

title: Forecasting sub-pixel vegetation potential shifts to guide restoration planning for the African Great Green Wall
data_and_method: Multi-task deep learning with CMIP6 outputs and habitat similarity
finding: Forecasts sub-pixel cover fractions (tree, other vegetation, bare ground). Potential for non-tree vegetation recovery is at least five times that of trees.

title: Deep Learning-based Uncertainty Quantification for spatio-temporal environmental Remote Sensing: A systematic literature review
finding: Abstract not read yet.
note: Systematic review of uncertainty quantification in deep learning for environmental remote sensing, per title.

title: Gobi Forage: An Early Warning System for Livestock in the Gobi Region of Mongolia
venue: Multifunctional Grasslands in a Changing World, Volume I (XXI International Grassland Congress)
data_and_method: Description of an early warning system: 297 monitoring sites in 8 Gobi provinces from 2004, the PHYGROW forage model driven by CMORPH satellite rainfall, model output combined with NDVI by geostatistics, and statistical forecasts 60 days ahead
finding: Started in 2004 with USAID funding. By 2007 the system mapped forage and its deviation from the long-term average every half month, with a 60-day forecast, shared by mail, internet and weekly national radio. It flagged severe drought in Gobi-Altai and Dundgobi in 2007, and a survey that October found the radio reports and maps useful to herders and local government.
note: Read in full, a one-page congress paper. Reports no skill score for the 60-day forecasts. vanlaere2026 cite a 2012 chapter on the system as the only forecast of pasture conditions they found.

title: Verification of a Forage Simulation Model Used for a Livestock Early Warning System in the Gobi Region of Mongolia
venue: Multifunctional Grasslands in a Changing World, Volume I (XXI International Grassland Congress)
data_and_method: PHYGROW forage model at 297 Gobi sites, driven by CMORPH rainfall and checked against biomass clipped 2 to 4 times per site; model output and NDVI combined by cokriging into maps every 15-16 days for 2005 and 2006, checked by cross-validation
finding: Modelled forage matched clipped biomass with R² 0.69 and a standard error of 83.6 kg/ha, under-predicting high biomass and over-predicting low. The cokriged maps gave R² 0.71 in cross-validation.
note: Read in full, a one-page congress paper. Tests the model of current forage and the maps, not the 60-day forecasts. The maps used only the sites where the model was validated. The 297-site field record could be ground truth for the Gobi if the data can be found.

title: Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
data_and_method: Review with simulations and case studies
finding: Random cross-validation underestimates error for data with spatial or temporal structure. Recommends blocking by space or time when the goal is prediction to new conditions.

title: Spatial validation reveals poor predictive performance of large-scale ecological mapping models
data_and_method: Random forest biomass model tested with random and spatial validation
finding: Random 10-fold cross-validation gave R2 0.53; spatial 44-fold gave 0.14; buffered leave-one-out fell to about 0.15 at 50 km and near zero beyond 100 km. A model using only coordinates did as well, so predictions came from location, not from the satellite and climate data.
note: For our design: estimate the spatial autocorrelation range of the target and hold out blocks larger than it.

title: Machine learning-based global maps of ecological variables and the challenge of assessing them
data_and_method: Commentary
finding: Discusses whether the quality of global machine-learning maps can be assessed, globally and locally.
